chunks: Do you not know that God's is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He will, and pardons whom He please, for God has the power over all things.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God's power to punish and pardon?
ai.summary: This verse from Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:40) serves as a divine response to the Jews' claim of exclusive sonship and power, asserting that all sovereignty belongs solely to Allah. It underscores the Shia theological principle of divine omnipotence (Qudrah) and free will (Ikhtiyar), where God's punishment and forgiveness are acts of His absolute choice rather than obligation. The verse reinforces the concept that while God is All-Powerful, His judgment is rooted in His wisdom and mercy.
